newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol may hit 4,800 ptas again by yr-end.
newsitem.headline: Repsol may hit 4,800 ptas again by yr-end.

text.p: Shares in Spanish energy group Repsol could rise to 4,700-4,800 pesetas before the end of the year, primarily boosted by the fact that they have underperformed the Ibex index for most of the year.

"It (Repsol) has been punished by the market because of results and it can't continue to lag (the market) so much. It's started to perform more reasonably. It could end the year around 4,700 or 4,750 pesetas," said Luis Prota, analyst at AB Asesores brokerage in Madrid.

At 1400 GMT, Repsol was up 90 pesetas, or two percent, to 4,585, while the Ibex-35 index of leading stocks was up 0.78 percent to 4,578.26. Repsol hit a low in January this year at 3,970 pesetas and a high in March of 4,880 pesetas.
Prota argued that the market has already discounted poor 1996 results, with most analysts forecasting a flat performance at best for the energy group for the full year.

In the nine months to September, Repsol posted a 5.6 percent fall in net attributable profit to 86.98 billion pesetas, with the operating performance heavily impacted by a slump in the chemicals division.
Operating income at the unit fell to 18.88 billion pesetas, versus 57.94 billion in the year-earlier period.
But next year's outlook looks better, analysts agreed. AB's Prota forecast an around eight percent climb in 1997 profit.
Javier Borrachero at Central Hispano brokerage agreed the share price should continue to recover.

"It'll carry on climbing. People have been upgrading their recommendations, and we in fact have revised ours to "buy" from "hold." What it does from now to the end of the year may depend on the Ibex but it's possible that it goes as far as 4,800 (pesetas) over one month," he said.
AB's Prota added that final investors may well be interested in Repsol because not only does it continue to look cheap compared to other major stocks, but also liquidity is good.
"Portfolios are full to the brim of three or four stocks. It could be that final investors want something to move into that looks cheap comparatively and doesn't have liquidity problems," he said.

With the government planning to sell its remaining 10 percent in Repsol on the bourse in early 1997, this is a key time for the shares, according to a trader at a Spanish bank who requested anonymity.
"Public interest in the placement is bound to be high, so the stock should be well-supported in the run-up," she said.
